title: Finite and infinite barrycades
summary: An $n$-barrycade of height $h$ is a set of $h$ permutations of $[n]$ such that all the prefix sums are different. This notion was described in 2020 by Richard Guy, together with the central problem to determine for which values of $n$ there exists a break-free $n$-barrycade, that is, one in which every possible prefix sum from $1$ to $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}-1$ is covered. The height of such barrycade would be $\frac{n+2}{2}$.
